questions.question: Distinguish between hard news and soft news
questions.solution_html:
• Hard News: All event centered news comes in the category of hard news. It is the
  • narration of any event that is reported immediately. It is factual stories with data that
  • is available for analysis. Issues of politics, war, economics and crime are considered
  • as hard news that come on the Front page of the daily. Example: A report on a
  • government policy change or a major international conflict.
  • Soft News: The other type of news goes beyond the event that has happened. It
  • analyses and interprets in order to arrive at logical conclusions. It generally includes
  • the background or human-interest stories, soft news often do not deal with serious
  • subjects. Example: A feature story on a celebrity's new movie or a piece on the latest
  • fashion trends.

questions.question: Describe the different types of media bias
questions.solution_html:
• Types of Media Bias
  •  Bias by omission: Bias by omission is when the reporter leaves out one side of
  • the argument, restricting the information that the consumer receives.
  •  Bias by selection of sources: Bias by selection of sources occurs when the author
  • includes multiple sources that only have to do with one side. Also, this can
  • occur when the author intentionally leaves out sources that are pertinent
  • to the other side of the story
  •  Bias by story selection: The second type of bias by selection is bias by story
  • selection. This is seen more throughout an entire corporation, rather than through
  • few stories. This occurs when news broadcasters only choose to include stories
  • that support the overall belief of the corporation in their broadcasts.
  •  Bias by placement: This type of bias shows how important a particular story is to
  • the reporter. Editors will choose to poorly place stories that they don’t think are as
  • important, or that they don’t want to be as easily accessible. This placement is
  • used to downplay their importance and make consumers think they aren’t as
  • important.
  •  Bias by labeling: Bias by labeling is a more complicated type of bias mostly used
  • to falsely describe politicians.

questions.question: Identify the key aspects that should be noted when covering a speech
questions.solution_html:
• Reporting on a Speech
  • Audience & Mood: Note the size, composition, and mood of the audience without
  • making subjective comments.
  • Speakers: Identify main speakers and anyone making significant points. Know their
  • names and titles beforehand or find out during the event.
  • Crowd Size: Estimate the crowd size by counting small groups and scaling up. Be
  • careful of biased estimates from police or organizers.
  • Accurate Notes: Take clear and accurate notes, focusing on important points. Use
  • shorthand or a tape recorder or other recording devices if necessary.
  • Prepared Speeches: Follow along with provided copies to catch any changes or
  • additions.
  • Balanced Reporting: Check outrageous claims and get responses to any accusations.
  • Finally, make sure that your story contains at least the following details
  •  The major point of the speech plus necessary background;
  •  The time, place and purpose of the meeting;
  •  Plenty of strong quotes;
  •  The size and composition of the audience, plus any important people in it;
  •  Audience reactions if they are significant.
questions.final_answer:  Audience reactions if they are significant

  • play a watchdog role in society by calling out such illicit activities and bringing them

  • and regulatory authorities. This involves pursuing and reporting on malpractices and
  • wrongdoing. Such reporting is all about making public stories that powerful forces
  • would prefer to keep secret.

questions.question: Discuss the ethical standards a journalist should keep in mind to maintain the professional conduct.
questions.solution_html:
• According to Press Council of India, a journalist should maintain follow certain
  • ethical norms such as
  • a) Accuracy and fairness: A journalist must inform, and comment on matters of
  • public interest, in a fair, accurate unbiased and decent manner. Inaccuracy and
  • personal remarks should always be avoided.
  • b) Prepublication Verification: Verification and checking of news before
  • publication is all the more necessary where its publication, and the comments based
  • thereon, can create complications.
  • c) Caution Against Defamatory Writings: Newspapers should not publish anything
  • which is per se defamatory or libelous against any individual or organization, unless
  • after due care and checking, they have sufficient reason to believe that it is true and
  • that its publication will be for public good.
  • d) Privacy: Intrusion or invasion on the privacy of individuals is not permissible
  • unless outweighed by genuine overriding public interest. While publishing names or
  • pictures of victims of sex crimes, great caution should be exercised.
  • e) Eschew Suggestive Guilt: Newspapers should eschew suggestive guilt by
  • association. They should not name or identify the family or relatives or associates of a
  • person convicted or accused of a crime when they are totally innocent and a reference
  • to them is not relevant to the matter reported.
  • f) Corrections: When any factual error or mistake is detected or confirmed, the
  • newspaper should publish the correction promptly, with due prominence and with an
  • apology or expression of regret in a case of serious lapse. He should also give due
  • weightage to the right of reply and to the letters to the Editor.
  • g) Communal Reports: Proper verification must be done before publishing reports
  • regarding communal clashes or disputes. The report should not vitiate the situation.
  • Instead, it should aim at soothing the ruffled feelings.
  • h) Sensational Headings: Sensational headings should be avoided. Headlines should
  • conform to the contents of news stories. They should be clear, unambiguous and
  • authentic.
  • i) Eschew Vulgarity and Obscenity: Obscene and vulgar items should be done away
  • with as these offend the public's good taste. Also, never glorify violence.
  • j) Avoid Crass Commercialism: In order to make profits, a newspaper should not
  • throw the ethics and journalistic values to the winds. Instead, it should try to create a
  • suitable equilibrium between objectivity and commercialism.
  • k) Avoid Caste, Religion or Community Disclosures: In general, a newspaper
  • should, not identify a person with his caste, religion or community.
  • l) Respect Confidence: If information is received from a source confidentially, the
  • confidence should be respected.

questions.question: Discuss the benefits of using inverted pyramid style in breaking news stories. Why is it regarded as an efficient way to communicate information?
questions.solution_html:
• Benefits of the Inverted Pyramid Style
  •  Prioritizes Crucial Information: This style ensures that the most important
  • information is delivered first. The lead contains the who, what, when, where, and
  • why, allowing readers to grasp the essential details quickly.
  •  Facilitates Quick Editing: Editors can easily trim stories from the bottom if space is
  • limited without losing the core information. This makes it highly practical for both
  • print and digital media.
  •  Enhances Reader Engagement: By presenting the key points right away, the
  • inverted pyramid style captures the reader's attention immediately. This is especially
  • important in an era where readers have shorter attention spans.
  •  Improves Search Engine Optimization (SEO): Online, this style helps with SEO as
  • it aligns with algorithms that prioritize articles where crucial information appears
  • early. It ensures that the content is indexed efficiently, making it more discoverable.
  •  Supports Breaking News: In fast-paced news situations, the inverted pyramid allows
  • for quick dissemination of vital information. It caters to audiences who need
  • immediate updates on ongoing events.
  • Why It Is Regarded as Efficient
  •  Clarity and Brevity: The inverted pyramid style ensures that the news is clear and
  • concise, which is critical when communicating urgent or complex issues.
  •  Flexibility for Updates: As new information comes in, updates can be added to the
  • existing article without restructuring the entire piece, maintaining the narrative's
  • integrity.
  •  Audience-Centric: This approach respects the reader's time, delivering the most
  • critical information upfront and allowing them to decide whether to read further for
  • additional details.

questions.question: Compare the writing styles used in traditional media versus new media

  • Formal Tone: Maintains a formal tone to uphold journalistic standards.
  • In-Depth Reporting: Provides detailed, well-researched stories.
  • Structured Format: Follows a structured format like the inverted pyramid style.
  • Editing Rigor: Undergoes multiple rounds of editing for accuracy.
  • Longer Pieces: Allows for comprehensive, longer articles.
  • New Media
  • Conversational Tone: Uses an informal, engaging tone.
  • Brevity and Conciseness: Delivers information quickly for short attention spans.
  • Multimedia Integration: Includes images, videos, and hyperlinks for a richer

questions.question: Discuss the ethical standards a journalist should keep in mind to maintain the professional conduct.
questions.solution_html:
• According to Press Council of India, a journalist should maintain follow certain
  • ethical norms such as
  • a) Accuracy and fairness: A journalist must inform, and comment on matters of
  • public interest, in a fair, accurate unbiased and decent manner. Inaccuracy and
  • personal remarks should always be avoided.
  • b) Prepublication Verification: Verification and checking of news before
  • publication is all the more necessary where its publication, and the comments based
  • thereon, can create complications.
  • c) Caution Against Defamatory Writings: Newspapers should not publish anything
  • which is per se defamatory or libelous against any individual or organization, unless
  • after due care and checking, they have sufficient reason to believe that it is true and
  • that its publication will be for public good.
  • d) Privacy: Intrusion or invasion on the privacy of individuals is not permissible
  • unless outweighed by genuine overriding public interest. While publishing names or
  • pictures of victims of sex crimes, great caution should be exercised.
  • e) Eschew Suggestive Guilt: Newspapers should eschew suggestive guilt by
  • association. They should not name or identify the family or relatives or associates of a
  • person convicted or accused of a crime when they are totally innocent and a reference
  • to them is not relevant to the matter reported.
  • f) Corrections: When any factual error or mistake is detected or confirmed, the
  • newspaper should publish the correction promptly, with due prominence and with an
  • apology or expression of regret in a case of serious lapse. He should also give due
  • weightage to the right of reply and to the letters to the Editor.
  • g) Communal Reports: Proper verification must be done before publishing reports
  • regarding communal clashes or disputes. The report should not vitiate the situation.
  • Instead, it should aim at soothing the ruffled feelings.
  • h) Sensational Headings: Sensational headings should be avoided. Headlines should
  • conform to the contents of news stories. They should be clear, unambiguous and
  • authentic.
  • i) Eschew Vulgarity and Obscenity: Obscene and vulgar items should be done away
  • with as these offend the public's good taste. Also, never glorify violence.
  • j) Avoid Crass Commercialism: In order to make profits, a newspaper should not
  • throw the ethics and journalistic values to the winds. Instead, it should try to create a

  • should, not identify a person with his caste, religion or community.
  • l) Respect Confidence: If information is received from a source confidentially, the
  • confidence should be respected.

questions.question: Discuss the benefits of using inverted pyramid style in breaking news stories. Why is it regarded as an efficient way to communicate information?
questions.solution_html:
• Benefits of the Inverted Pyramid Style
  •  Prioritizes Crucial Information: This style ensures that the most important
  • information is delivered first. The lead contains the who, what, when, where, and
  • why, allowing readers to grasp the essential details quickly.
  •  Facilitates Quick Editing: Editors can easily trim stories from the bottom if space is
  • limited without losing the core information. This makes it highly practical for both
  • print and digital media.
  •  Enhances Reader Engagement: By presenting the key points right away, the
  • inverted pyramid style captures the reader's attention immediately. This is especially
  • important in an era where readers have shorter attention spans.
  •  Improves Search Engine Optimization (SEO): Online, this style helps with SEO as
  • it aligns with algorithms that prioritize articles where crucial information appears
  • early. It ensures that the content is indexed efficiently, making it more discoverable.
  •  Supports Breaking News: In fast-paced news situations, the inverted pyramid allows
  • for quick dissemination of vital information. It caters to audiences who need
  • immediate updates on ongoing events.
  • Why It Is Regarded as Efficient
  •  Clarity and Brevity: The inverted pyramid style ensures that the news is clear and
  • concise, which is critical when communicating urgent or complex issues.
  •  Flexibility for Updates: As new information comes in, updates can be added to the
  • existing article without restructuring the entire piece, maintaining the narrative's
  • integrity.
  •  Audience-Centric: This approach respects the reader's time, delivering the most
  • critical information upfront and allowing them to decide whether to read further for
  • additional details.
